harnessDoctorDegradedReason: The local file install exposed a runnable npx harness, but doctor reported cli-build degraded because harness/cli/dist/index.js was not built in the source tree.
summary: Ran the full harness setup flow against the fresh Cobra clone without using the interactive router. The local harness core installed and `harness doctor --json` produced a parseable Envelope; the harnessability assessment graded the repo B with Operate-Today B (74%) and Adaptability B (70%), so the abandonment gate did not trip. I hand-wrote the BIO governance document, used the add-extension flow to scaffold and fill a `boot` verb, independently verified `doctor`, `help`, and `harness boot --json`, and recorded a retro via `harness record retro`.

retrospective.workedWell: Repo-local skill discovery was clear through `minih skills doctor`, the Cobra repo was a strong candidate for the flow because `go test ./...` is a clean library health signal, `harness new boot --wrap "go test ./..."` produced a loadable extension scaffold, and `harness boot --json` returned an honest ok Envelope after the handler was filled.
retrospective.confusing: The install recipe did not account for non-Node repos with no package.json, so plain `npm install <harnessSource>` selected /tmp as the npm prefix. The local harness doctor also reported a degraded cli-build layer even though the installed `npx harness` command worked, and the assessment skill is currently a contract/instruction rather than a single executable report writer.
retrospective.magicWand: Ship a headless `harness setup --repo <path> --boot "go test ./..." --json` command that handles repo-local npm prefixing, writes the harnessability reports, generates `.harness/engineering-harness.md`, scaffolds/fills/verifies `boot`, and returns all authored paths in one Envelope.

coordination.notes: No peer coordination was involved in this single-shot run.

difficulties.description: The documented local install command `npm install $MINIH_PROJECT_ROOT` is unsafe in a Go repo with no package.json because npm chose /tmp as the prefix and tried to write /private/tmp/node_modules instead of the target clone.
difficulties.mitigation: Used `npm install --prefix . /Users/jordanknight/substrate/harness-engineering --no-audit --no-fund` so node_modules stayed inside the target clone.

difficulties.description: `harness doctor --json` stayed degraded after installation because the local file install pointed at a harness source tree whose `harness/cli/dist/index.js` was not built, even though the npx harness command itself worked.
difficulties.mitigation: Treated the parseable doctor Envelope and working CLI as sufficient for the install sanity check while recording the degraded cli-build layer.

difficulties.description: The harnessability assessment skill is guidance-only in this CLI context; it does not expose a single command that writes the required report, so the agent had to manually produce the skill's report artifacts while following the skill contract.
difficulties.mitigation: Used the skill schema/template instructions and independently read `.harness/reports/harnessability/latest.json` after writing the reports.

difficulties.description: The flow requires governance to be hand-written because no `harness init` writer is shipped yet, which forces agents to copy the BIO contract manually.
difficulties.mitigation: Read the governance template and hand-wrote `.harness/engineering-harness.md` with all eight BIO fields.

difficulties.description: `harness new boot --wrap` produced a loadable stub with a placeholder summary and hard error behavior on wrapped command failure, so it was not yet an honest boot Envelope for degraded test failures.
difficulties.mitigation: Edited the scaffolded file to add a real summary, include command/exit/duration/stdout/stderr data, and return `ctx.degraded` with a next_action when tests fail.

difficulties.description: The required output instructions say difficulty IDs should be VF-NNN, while the generic schema example says MH-NNN, creating conflicting numbering guidance.
difficulties.mitigation: Used VF-NNN as the task-specific rule because it was explicit for this validate-harness-flow run.
